task: Make GET /v1/analytics/cli-analytics/sessions page, search and sort in Postgres (page IDs first, then details), add a safe started_at index migration verified with EXPLAIN, and cap per-request concurrent DB connections, keeping response shape, money and filters unchanged.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the reader adapter (get_session_page, possibly _sessions_cte), the CliAnalyticsReader port and SESSION_PAGE_SORTS, filters.restricted_to, the handler get_sessions (pricing and framework paths), a per-request connection limiter around the shared asyncpg pool/engine, and a new Alembic revision. That is 4 or more components over repository, service and schema, and the existing in-SQL paging path is a clear pattern to extend.

Core goals are stated, but the ticket's own open questions (framework filtering, unpriced-model metadata, SLA, connection management) are design decisions that remain open. Moving the cost_usd sort into SQL conflicts with catalog pricing that lives in Python. The stored delivery_framework can be NULL or stale compared with read-time classification. The two paths match search differently (served/cleaned prompt vs ILIKE), and the handler line references in the ticket are out of date.

The closest pattern is the existing get_session_page plus the restricted_to SQL path and its live parity tests. It does not cover the cost_usd sort, the framework filter, a whole-window total count, or the cost of the _activity_cte probes. There is no precedent for building an index on a populated, frequently updated session_dims table: the migration runner wraps everything in one transaction (transactional_ddl=True), so CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run as-is, and a plain build takes a SHARE lock that blocks refresher writes. No limiter for pool concurrency exists. The task is performance-critical with an 825 ms target.

About 8-10 modified files (reader.py, ports.py, filters.py, the handler, engine/settings/config for the concurrency cap, the storage guide, test_reader, handler tests, test_migrations, live session-page test) plus 2-3 new ones (migration revision, EXPLAIN/plan or concurrency tests), spread across repository, service, external/alembic and tests.
Service, Repository/DB-Persistence with a schema index migration, and Infrastructure (the connection pool shared with ingest and background jobs). The API contract stays fixed.
